idiom_name: init(repo: some OrderRepository) + construction in the App entry point
implementation_notes: Swift's default realization is a protocol for the seam plus an initializer parameter for the injection: init(repo: OrderRepository) stores the value, and the app entry point (@main type, App struct, or a composition-root factory) builds the graph. What replaces the injector is that root plus Swift's value semantics - structs copied into consumers, classes shared by reference - with @EnvironmentKey/@EnvironmentValues covering SwiftUI's view-tree injection. Swinject and Factory are optional and add registration plus property wrappers when the graph outgrows hand wiring.
pitfalls: Existential boxing (`any OrderRepository`) costs dynamic dispatch; on hot paths prefer a generic parameter (some OrderRepository / <R: OrderRepository>).
View controllers instantiated by storyboards cannot be constructor-injected - property injection plus initCompleted wiring is the fallback.
Retain cycles when an injected service holds the consumer (delegates, closures) - use weak captures deliberately.

variants.name: Swinject runtime container
variants.implementation_notes: Swinject is the classic Swift container: container.register(Animal.self) { _ in Cat() } pairs a protocol with a factory closure that resolves its own dependencies through the passed resolver, and object scopes control lifetimes; consumers are pulled with resolve(Animal.self). It reproduces the full classic injector structure in a language without reflection and supports storyboard-driven property injection via initCompleted. Choose it for large UIKit apps where construction is spread over storyboards and app delegates.
pitfalls: resolve returns an optional and force-unwrapping turns a missing registration into a crash at that call site.
Overlapping registrations: the last registration for a type wins unless named - use registration names for variants.

variants.name: Factory keypath containers with @Injected property wrappers
variants.idiom_name: Factory<T> keypath definitions on a Container + @Injected(\.service)
variants.implementation_notes: Factory replaces the runtime container with keypath-typed factories: each dependency is a computed Factory property on a Container extension returning an instance, and @Injected(\.service) property wrappers resolve it on initialization with compile-time safety (a missing factory is a compile error). Scopes (.singleton/.cached/.shared) and context-based overrides provide container features without a resolve lookup, and the wrappers integrate with SwiftUI and actor isolation. It is the modern, storyboard-free alternative to Swinject.
pitfalls: Property wrappers resolve at initialization; a dependency that must change later needs DynamicInjected or an explicit reset.
Factories capturing the shared container transitively can create long-lived references - scope them deliberately (.cached/.singleton).
